key_highlights: ASX finished higher as oil prices and bond yields eased; big four banks (CBA, ANZ, NAB, WBC) advanced on softer rate expectations
AUD crushed after Fed failed 'Warshach test', pressuring export-oriented ASX miners and resources names
IMF urged Australian government to cut spending ahead of another RBA rate hike, raising fiscal and monetary tightening concerns
WA exploration pipeline bright: Dalaroo copper-nickel-PGE targets, Critica 58% rare earths carbonate, Augustus 30g/t gold drill
Anthropic secured $31bn datacentre deal in western Queensland, signalling major AI infrastructure buildout in Australia
Qantas ground staff strike looms over 'Joyce-era' bargaining, threatening QAN.AX operations and consumer sentiment
Coles (WES.AX) maintains elevated milk prices despite axing farmer support, fuelling cost-of-living pressure
Bathla collapse triggers insolvency storm; private credit exposure to rich-listers flagged as systemic risk
Fuel supply crunch at east-coast ports threatens energy distribution margins
ACCC moves to break real estate agency monopoly, potential tailwind for REITs and property sector

sectors.trend: Big four banks advanced as oil and bond yields eased, supporting net interest margin expectations. However, soaring state interest costs and IMF spending-cut warnings create fiscal headwinds. Private credit risk (Bathla insolvency) adds credit-cycle concern.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, ANZ.AX, NAB.AX, WBC.AX benefit from yield curve normalisation but face elevated credit-loss provisions if private credit defaults spread. Monitor NIM trajectory vs. RBA path.

sectors.trend: AUD weakness supports export earnings for BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX. WA exploration pipeline (Dalaroo Cu-Ni-PGE, Critica rare earths, Augustus gold) signals long-term supply growth. Oil easing pressures energy-linked miners.
sectors.implications: Short-term AUD headwind offsets commodity price support. Rare earths and PGE names (Critica, Dalaroo) offer thematic upside tied to energy transition. Gold grades (Augustus, Aguia) support GSG.AX, WES.AX gold peers.

sectors.trend: Oil prices eased, pressuring CSG and oil producers. Fuel supply crunch at east-coast ports threatens distribution margins. Coal policy debate (Albo government) and green hydrogen spending scrutiny add regulatory uncertainty.
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, WEL.AX, SXG.AX face margin pressure from softer oil. Fuel distributors (AUS.AX, VGE.AX) exposed to supply disruption. Coal transition risk weighs on BHP.AX thermal coal segment.

sectors.trend: Qantas strike threat, Coles milk pricing, fashion brand collapses (Cue, Veronika Maine), and backpacker cuts hit tourism/farming. Real wage growth crushed by exploited workers. Tenants see rent relief.
sectors.implications: QAN.AX faces operational disruption risk. WES.AX, WES.AX pricing power under scrutiny. Tourism-linked names (SOL.AX, LYC.AX) pressured by backpacker cuts. REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) may benefit from tenant relief.

sectors.trend: Anthropic $31bn QLD datacentre deal signals major AI capex in Australia. Labor's new AI rules (smart glasses ban) and AI job-displacement debate create regulatory uncertainty. News Corp AI content generation signals sector-wide adoption.
sectors.implications: Datacentre and infrastructure names (WBC.AX, VNT.AX, STO.AX) benefit from AI capex cycle. Regulatory risk for AI hardware. Long-term structural tailwind for Australian cloud/infrastructure spend.

sectors.trend: ACCC real estate monopoly challenge could reshape agency economics. Trump policy mulls crashing Aussie house prices. Tenants catching a break suggests rent stabilisation.
sectors.implications: GPW.AX, ICPS.AX, DGL.AX may see improved tenant retention. Agency fee reform could compress REIT operating costs. House price risk is a medium-term overhang.

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to consolidate near recent highs with volatility around Fed decision and Qantas strike. Banks and miners support the index; consumer and energy sectors lag. AUD weakness is a two-edged sword – supports exporters but pressures import costs and consumer spending. Expect 1-2% range-bound trading in ^AXJO over next 2-3 weeks.
market_outlook.long_term: Medium-term outlook constructive for ASX 200 driven by AI infrastructure capex (Anthropic QLD), WA critical minerals pipeline, and bank NIM recovery. Headwinds from RBA tightening, state interest costs, immigration-driven labour constraints, and private credit stress. 6-12 month view: modest 5-8% upside for ^AXJO if RBA pauses and commodity prices stabilise.
